findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that a failed quarantine copy MUST abort the restore (skip the destructive `git checkout`) and fall back to `git merge --abort` + keep-local, so local bytes are never destroyed unpreserved; add a test that a copy failure leaves the worktree modification intact.
evidence: Plan: 'the local bytes are preserved in quarantine, the HEAD bytes unblock the merge'
AC: 'A worktree modification named by the abort is preserved byte-for-byte in the quarantine directory before restore'
ABSENCE: no stated behavior when the quarantine copy itself errors before the destructive checkout
findings.finding: For the modification path, the plan orders quarantine-copy before `git checkout -- <path>` (which destroys the local bytes), but does not state that the restore must be aborted if the quarantine copy fails. If the copy silently fails (disk full, permission, path length) and checkout proceeds, the local working-tree bytes are lost with no preservation — contradicting the AC that they be preserved byte-for-byte.
findings.location: Approach — 'a working-tree MODIFICATION is first copied into the same quarantine directory ... and then restored via git checkout'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: verify the quarantine copy succeeded (exists + byte-identical) before running `git checkout -- <path>`; on copy failure, do NOT checkout — fall through to the existing abort/keep-local path.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fence the restore to the UNSTAGED case (index==HEAD) the plan actually reasons about: gate on the porcelain SECOND column (` D`/` M`) and treat any first-column staged status (`D `/`M `/etc.) or ambiguous state as a fall-through to today's abort-keep-local-hint-fsck path, so the 'content already at HEAD' safety claim is guaranteed true wherever `git checkout -- <path>` runs.
evidence: `git checkout -- <path>` restores the worktree from the INDEX, not from HEAD; the 'content already at HEAD' claim only holds when index==HEAD (unstaged case)

compact_txn.py:255-270 `_retire_folded_sources` uses os.rename with `git add -A`/commit only later (compact_txn.py:461), so the named recurrence leaves UNSTAGED ` D` deletions — but the plan generalizes beyond that to 'a working-tree MODIFICATION' without qualifying the porcelain first column
e72e recurrence comment: '119 entries, all ` D <ticket>/.archived` (unstaged worktree deletions)' — confirms the modeled case is unstaged, i.e. the staged case is un-tested and un-handled
sync.py:248-269 `_quarantine_untracked` returns False (safe abort) when any path is missing; the plan's deletion arm has no analogous move-before-mutate copy
findings.finding: The plan's safety invariant for the deletion arm — `git checkout -- <path>` restores 'the HEAD bytes' / 'content already at HEAD — nothing can be lost' — only holds when the index matches HEAD. `git checkout -- <path>` restores from the INDEX, not HEAD. The plan detects only an UNSTAGED worktree deletion (` D`) and an unqualified 'modification', and does not fence out STAGED changes (porcelain first-column `D `/`M `). For a staged deletion/modification the checkout restores the staged (non-HEAD) bytes, the retry re-aborts, and in the deletion arm the local bytes are overwritten with NO quarantine copy taken (quarantine is only on the modification arm) — a silent, non-recoverable failure that also does not cleanly fall back to today's abort-keep-local behavior.
findings.location: Approach — 'a working-tree DELETION of a tracked file (git status --porcelain reports ` D`) is restored non-destructively via git checkout -- <path> (content already at HEAD — nothing can be lost)'
scenarios: An interrupted fold that had already run `git add -A` on the retired-source deletion before dying leaves a STAGED deletion (`D `); reconverge restores from the index (still deleted), retry re-aborts, and no quarantine copy protects the bytes
A staged modification (`M `) named by the abort: checkout restores staged bytes, merge re-aborts, recovery silently no-ops
findings.suggested_fix: In the plan text, restrict the deletion/modification arms to `git status --porcelain` entries whose WORKTREE column is `D`/`M` while the STAGED column is unmodified (` `), i.e. index==HEAD so `git checkout -- <path>` provably restores HEAD bytes; route staged or otherwise-ambiguous statuses to the unchanged `git merge --abort` + fsck-recover fallback.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State (and ideally test) how a working tree carrying BOTH the untracked-overwrite and the local-changes abort classes at once is handled — either detect/repair both classes before the single retry, or explicitly document that the second class self-heals on the next reconverge round.
evidence: Plan Context explicitly notes the rename yields BOTH a tracked deletion AND an untracked creation, i.e. both abort classes can be live at once
sync.py:194-223 shows the single-retry budget the plan inherits; git's unpack-trees reports one 'would be overwritten' category per attempt
The plan's Testing/AC do not include a fixture where both classes co-occur
findings.finding: The plan retries the merge exactly ONCE per _union_merge call and handles the two abort classes (variant (a) untracked-overwrite, variant (b) local-changes) as separate detection branches, but git reports only one abort category per `git merge` attempt. An interrupted rename can co-produce BOTH an untracked `*.retired` creation (variant a) AND a tracked source deletion (variant b) simultaneously; a single pass can therefore clear only one class, and the plan does not state whether the second class is expected to self-heal on a subsequent reconverge round.
findings.location: Approach — 'Then retry the merge once.'; Context — 'a rename of a tracked file is a tracked deletion + an untracked creation'
scenarios: An interrupted compaction leaves both an untracked `*-SNAPSHOT.json`/`*.retired` collision and a tracked-source ` D` deletion; the first _union_merge clears one class and the retry aborts on the other
